newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's new Global Bank hopes to open in 1997 Q1.
newsitem.headline: Manila's new Global Bank hopes to open in 1997 Q1.

text.p: Global Bank, a subsidiary of Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, is finalising its list of shareholders to include foreign groups and hopes to start operation by the first quarter of next year, Metrobank said.

Metrobank president Antonio Abacan said Global would seek an extension of an October 23 deadline the Central Bank had given it to submit the final requirements before it could get its banking license.
"We will request for another three months," Abacan said.

The Central Bank's policy-making Monetary Board last year approved Global's application to operate but the start of its operation had been delayed by a change in the composition of its shareholders and in the bank's name from the original Hemisphere Banking Corp.

Metrobank plans to own 49 percent of Global Bank, with local and Hong Kong investors owning 10 percent each, Abacan told reporters. The remaining 30 percent is to be owned by groups that could include Japanese and Taiwanese businessmen, he said.

Central Bank officials said the delay was partly caused by the processing of the requirements of a prospective Japanese bank shareholder. They said the Japanese bank had to seek permission from Japan's Ministry of Finance before it could put money into a Philippine bank.
There are 50 commercial banks operating in the Philipines.
